clue.text: Flags for US naval officers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: banners flown by ships to show nationality
second meaning: the lowest commissioned rank in the American navy

explanation.surface: Someone is ordering pennants to hand out to American navy officers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a ship's national banner and the most junior commissioned rank in the American navy.

clue.text: Once modelled naked

parts.note: ex means former, what once was
a model poses

explanation.surface: An artist's model who used to sit unclothed.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposed means uncovered and open to view, which fits naked as a near synonym.

clue.text: Back front-runner, one in with a chance of winning

definitions.text: one in with a chance of winning

parts.note: to back a proposal is to second it
the front-runner in a race is the favourite

explanation.surface: A tipster urges you to bet on the leading horse, a likely winner.
explanation.walkthrough: Back looks like betting advice but means support a motion.
explanation.definitionFit: The runner rated just behind the market leader by bookmakers still has a real prospect of victory.

clue.text: Tropical fish strung out

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Fish from the tropics hung out on a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Grunts are warm-water marine fish named for the grunting noises they make with their teeth.

clue.text: Wears this, possibly, on completion of sprint?

definitions.text: Wears this, possibly, on completion of sprint?

indicators.note: possibly means the letters might form something else when rearranged

parts.note: nine letters to rearrange

indicators.note: completion is the finish, so only the final letter of the next word counts

parts.note: its final letter

explanation.surface: A runner pulls on a top after finishing a dash.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the last letter of sprint joins the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose cotton jersey that athletes typically put on over sportswear after exercising to keep warm.

clue.text: Reuse on bike

parts.note: re means 'on the subject of', so on gives RE
a bike is a cycle

explanation.surface: Someone is putting old material to new use on a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: To recycle something is to process waste so the material can serve again, a direct synonym of reuse.

clue.text: Reportedly authentic Scottish dance

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so go by sound

parts.note: authentic means genuine

explanation.surface: Claims that a highland dance is the genuine article.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a lively traditional folk dance of Scotland, performed in a set of couples.

clue.text: Taxi goes round almost all of US port to find burial place

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: almost all means the whole word except its last letter

parts.note: Tacoma is a port city in Washington State

explanation.surface: A cab drives around a city in the American north-west hunting for a cemetery.
explanation.definitionFit: A catacomb is an underground cemetery of tunnels with recesses for tombs.

clue.text: Barrier in road one racist vandalised

indicators.note: something vandalised is smashed up, so the letters are broken and rearranged

parts.note: fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A roadblock defaced by a bigot.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase means a sanitary cordon, originally a line set up to stop disease spreading.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a guarded line or buffer zone isolating an area, so it is a kind of barrier.

clue.text: Unpredictable King, in time, gets a twitch

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: an era is a period of time
R is short for rex, Latin for king
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A monarch develops a nervous spasm in due course.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic behaviour is irregular and inconsistent, so it cannot be foreseen.

clue.text: I may help one to see painting in a different light

definitions.text: I may help one to see painting in a different light

parts.words: I may help one to see painting in a different light
parts.note: surface reading: an art critic or lighting expert who changes how you view a canvas
setter's reading: literally, someone who cleans old varnish and grime off a canvas so it looks brighter

explanation.surface: A speaker claims to make people reconsider artworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a different light' sounds like a fresh opinion, but it is meant literally: cleaning a dirty canvas makes it look lighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a specialist removes discoloured varnish and repairs damage so an old work looks as its artist intended.

clue.text: Great goodness — it can spread in place of debauchery

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another, signalled by this placing word
things spread out are scattered, so the letters are laid out in a new order

parts.note: these five letters rearranged
a sty is a pigsty, figuratively a place of filth and debauchery

explanation.surface: A moralist warns that holiness can spread into a den of vice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In place of' reads as 'instead of', but here 'in' is the containment signal and 'place of debauchery' is the pigsty.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanctity is the state of being holy, which is goodness of the highest degree.

clue.text: Confront one about charge

parts.note: a means one
c is short for circa, Latin for about
a charge is a cost or price

explanation.surface: Someone challenges a person over a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost is to approach and address someone boldly or aggressively, which is to confront them.

clue.text: Not the sort of music associated with steel or brass bands?

definitions.text: Not the sort of music associated with steel or brass bands?

parts.words: Not the sort of music associated with steel or brass bands?
parts.note: surface reading: a style unlike Caribbean steel drums or colliery brass bands
setter's reading: steel and brass are both weighty alloys, yet this loud rock genre has nothing to do with those bands

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that steel and brass are dense alloys, yet bands named for them play nothing like this loud guitar rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud, aggressive rock genre built on distorted electric guitars and pounding drums.

clue.text: Foolish plan — rook must be lost

indicators.note: something lost is taken away, so one letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a draft is a preliminary plan
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A stupid scheme in which a chess piece has to be sacrificed.
explanation.definitionFit: Daft is an informal British word for silly or stupid, so it matches foolish closely.

clue.text: What's usually covered in bars?

parts.note: surface reading: something found in pubs, such as a counter covered with drinks
setter's reading: the measures into which written music is divided, filling each printed page

explanation.walkthrough: Bars suggests pubs or prison; here they are the divisions of a musical score printed on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed musical notation on loose pages is laid out in bars, short measures separated by vertical lines.

clue.text: US theatre may give boy award

indicators.note: may give suggests the letters could produce another word once rearranged

parts.note: eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An American playhouse might present a young actor with a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York avenue lends its name to the district of major commercial theatres in Manhattan.

clue.text: This may get one a run in foremost of cars with a very high gear

definitions.text: This may get one a run

indicators.note: foremost means the very front, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

parts.note: its opening letter
overdrive is a gear above top, for cruising at speed

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a motorist with a car in a very high gear going for a drive.
explanation.walkthrough: A cover drive is a cricket stroke played through the off side, past the fielding position called cover; it may earn the batter a run.
explanation.definitionFit: A batting stroke in cricket is something that may score runs, and this is a classic attacking stroke.

clue.text: Reticent person with drink abruptly stops talking

parts.note: someone who keeps quiet is called a clam
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A shy person with a glass suddenly falls silent.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to refuse suddenly to say any more, shutting up like a bivalve.

clue.text: Responsibility taken on board by son, usually

indicators.note: something taken on board is carried within, so the letters lie inside the following words

parts.note: runs across the two words

explanation.surface: A son usually ends up shouldering a duty.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or duty that falls on someone, a direct synonym of responsibility.

clue.text: Piece of steak with egg on for naval doctor

indicators.note: a piece is a small bit, here just the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: its opening letter
to egg someone on is to urge them on

explanation.surface: A cook serves a cut of beef topped with a fried egg for the ship's medic.
explanation.walkthrough: Egg on looks like a topping but is a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: On ships the medical officer is traditionally titled by this surgical rank rather than called a doctor.

clue.text: Contemporary Royal Navy following current fashion

indicators.note: following places the first-named piece behind the next one in the final order

parts.note: the mode is the prevailing style
the standard abbreviation for the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Today's navy keeps up with the latest trends.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe things belonging to the present day rather than the past.

clue.text: A pair, returning, notice mountain sheep

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a duo is a pair
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: Two people coming back spot a notice.
explanation.definitionFit: The aoudad, or Barbary sheep, is a wild sheep of the North African mountains.

clue.text: One who brings in ale after one's married

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the others in the final order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one, with the possessive joining it to the next word
M is the standard abbreviation for married
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: Someone orders a beer once they have got married.
explanation.definitionFit: An importer is a trader who brings goods into a country from abroad.

clue.text: Room mostly used for card game

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a study is a room for reading and work

explanation.surface: A room that is generally set aside for playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Stud is a form of poker in which some of each player's cards are dealt face up.

clue.text: Submit to majority opinion and bathe down river, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an idiom for going along with what most people think
second meaning, taken literally: swimming in the direction the current flows

explanation.surface: Someone conforms and then takes a dip downstream.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second half is the idiom read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to conform with prevailing views, from the ease of swimming along with the current.

clue.text: Greek character, we hear, looked on, drunk

indicators.note: we hear means the clue is going by what is spoken, not what is written

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: A Greek figure stood watching a drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Pie-eyed is informal slang for intoxicated, describing someone who has had far too much alcohol.

clue.text: Light tail of gull (an aquatic bird)

indicators.note: the tail is the very end, so only the final letter of the next word counts

parts.note: its final letter
taken as written
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Describes a pale tail feather on a gull, a sea bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp in a protective case, so it is a source of light.
